input.quote: Under no circumstances shall any Party be liable to any other Party in contract, tort, (including negligence or breach of statutory duty) or otherwise for loss (whether direct or indirect) of profits, property, traffic, business or anticipated savings, or for any indirect or consequential loss or damage in connection with the operation of this Agreement howsoever caused.
input.rationale:
The liability regime sits at the fallback on its material terms and is not redlined. (1) Mutuality: Paragraph 21.3 (p0242-p0245) binds "any Party" in favour of "any other Party" — the exclusion of indirect/consequential loss, lost profits, property, traffic, business and anticipated savings (including for delay, damage to or failure of APCN 2 and service interruption) applies symmetrically to Teleglobe USA and to every other APCN 2 Party, so there is no one-sided protection and no walk-away asymmetry. (2) Carve-outs: this is a multilateral consortium C&MA with no aggregate monetary cap anywhere in the document (confirmed by searches for cap/aggregate/limited-to-the-amount and review of Paragraphs 4.9, 21, 23, 31, 32 and 33). Because no cap exists, direct liability for indemnification obligations (21.2, p0241), breach of the Paragraph 31 confidentiality covenant, gross negligence and wilful misconduct is already uncapped — the four fallback carve-out elements are satisfied by the structure rather than by express wording. (3) The one element short of the checklist is a stated mutual cap "based on 12 months of fees": there is no vendor/customer fee stream here (costs are APCN 2 Capital Costs and O&M Costs allocated per Schedule B), so a fees-based cap has no basis to attach to. In its place the Agreement gives Teleglobe two meaningful and mutual limitations: liability is "several and not joint or collective" (21.1, p0240), and third-party claim exposure, indemnities and post-termination liabilities are limited to each Party's Schedule B proportion (21.2, 32.1, 32.5, 32.6). Noted for the file, not flagged: no USD 1,000,000 floor, no "fees paid or payable" basis, no express Excluded Claims list, and no statement that payment obligations are outside the cap — all preferred-only mechanics. We would not seek to introduce an aggregate cap here, since inserting one into a symmetric consortium regime would cap the other Parties' exposure to us as much as ours to them.</parationale>
